To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the leakage current of a CZT sample is proportional to the surface sheet resistance and the area of the electrode, and that the surface leakage current is independent of the electrode configuration.

the leakage current of a device with two electrodes is determined by the surface sheet resistance and the electrode geometry, that the leakage current is independent of the applied voltage, and that the surface sheet resistance is a function of the electrode configuration, the electrode size and shape, the sample size and shape, and the surface passivation technique.

1) the surface sheet resistance is directly proportional to the applied potential; 2) the surface sheet current is inversely proportional to the applied DC potential; 3) the surface sheet resistances of devices with the same surface layer thickness, but different sample sizes, can be compared; 4) the surface sheet currents of devices with the surface layer thickness and the sample size held constant, but with different electrode configurations, can be compared.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement and modeling of leakage currents in high resistivity semiconductors.
the development of models which can be used to quantitate the leakage current in CZT detectors.
the measurement and modeling of surface leakage currents in high resistivity semiconductor detectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the surface sheet resistance is not directly related to the leakage current density, and that the surface sheet resistances measured for the same material using different geometrical configurations are not directly comparable.
, for a given electrode configuration, a device which is used to measure leakage currents should be designed such that the surface sheet resistance is much larger than the bulk resistance.
the leakage current is not simply a function of the surface sheet resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the surface sheet resistance is not a constant for a given passivation technique, but rather is a function of sample size and shape, and electrode configuration.
the leakage current is a function of the surface sheet resistance, the applied electric field and the electrode geometry.
the leakage current is not a constant, but rather is dependent on the electrode configuration.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the leakage current in CZT devices is not only dependent on the resistivities of the surface and bulk material but also on geometrical factors such as the electrode size and spacing and sample dimensions.
a simple model can be used to predict the leakage current for the case of a planar device with a circular contact.
the leakage current measured across a CZT sample can be dominated by the surface leakage currents, and that these currents are sensitive to the electrode configuration.
